summary: Added a deterministic DOCX style profile and OOXML styles.xml generation for export_docx. The export remains backwards compatible while supporting an optional style_profile override and now writes word/styles.xml, the styles content type, and a document relationship to the styles part. This is a stdlib-only GB/T 9704-2012-inspired style skeleton, not full formal layout certification.
implemented: backend/server.py: added _bounded_int(raw, default, minimum, maximum) for conservative numeric style normalization.

backend/server.py: added build_docx_style_profile(payload_or_options=None), returning method=docx_style_profile_v1 with A4 page, margins, font hints, paragraph settings, style IDs, and footer page-number metadata.
backend/server.py: added docx_style_xml(profile) and supporting OOXML paragraph helpers.

export_docx(title, body, style_profile=None) remains compatible with old two-argument calls and now writes styled title/body paragraphs, word/styles.xml, content type override, and word/_rels/document.xml.rels.
/api/export/docx now forwards optional payload['style_profile'] to export_docx.
tools/run_quality_gates.py py-compile gate now includes tests/test_docx_style_profile.py.
README.md and docs/ROADMAP.md document the v1 boundary.

risks: The style profile is a deterministic OOXML skeleton only; formal official-document layout still needs later slices for page furniture, headings, tables, attachments, seals/signatures, and visual validation.
Body paragraphs are styled uniformly as MaterialBody in v1; semantic section/heading detection is intentionally deferred.
Font names are hints in OOXML and final rendering depends on fonts installed on the user's system.
